guide.title: Mozart: String Quartet No. 19 in C major, K. 465 – I. Adagio (listening guide)
guide.overview: The home key is C major. This guide follows the movement in four parts: a slow opening (Part 1), a faster main section marked Allegro, a long third part, and a short closing part. Keys and chords here are estimated by computer, so treat them as a good guide, not as certain. The score is of good quality, but the "who leads" labels are a rough guess. Listen for the change from the quiet, searching opening to the brisker Allegro. Then listen for the return to C major at the end, and the very soft (pp) final measures.

listening_points.headline: The viola begins, softly
listening_points.text: The movement opens quietly, with the viola in front [m. 1]. The others accompany it. The key is estimated as G major here.

listening_points.headline: First violin steps forward
listening_points.text: The first violin leads in [m. 2-6]. The four lines move fairly independently at first [m. 2]. A marked crescendo (a gradual rise in loudness) leads to a loud moment at [m. 4]. Then it drops suddenly back to soft at [m. 5].

listening_points.headline: New keys: F major, then C minor
listening_points.text: The music moves to F major [m. 6-9], then to C minor [m. 10-14]. Minor keys often sound more serious. The first violin probably leads in much of this stretch. In the C minor stretch, the lead is unclear and shared. A crescendo builds to a louder moment at [m. 13].

listening_points.headline: Back in G major, with sharp accents
listening_points.text: G major returns at [m. 15-21]. The music is soft, with sudden sharp accents marked sf (a strong, short push on a note) [m. 16-21]. The lead is shared and unclear. The section ends at [m. 22] in C major, with all parts moving together (homophonic).

listening_points.headline: The Allegro begins: a clear tune in C major
listening_points.text: The faster Allegro starts softly in C major [m. 23]. The first violin has a clear tune, and the others accompany it [m. 23-30]. This is one of the plainest stretches in the movement. The whole Allegro is marked to be repeated.

listening_points.headline: Loud, busy interplay between the parts
listening_points.text: The volume jumps suddenly to loud at [m. 31]. The parts now play independent lines, so no single tune stands out. A sharp accent falls at [m. 35]. Then it drops suddenly to soft at [m. 36].

listening_points.headline: Soft tune returns, then a loud C major moment
listening_points.text: The first violin leads again, softly, with accompaniment [m. 38-42]. A loud touch arrives at [m. 43]. Then it is soft again [m. 44-46].

listening_points.headline: Shifts through G major, D major and A minor
listening_points.text: The key moves to G major [m. 47], then to D major [m. 53], then to A minor [m. 60]. Loud and soft alternate quickly. A crescendo is marked at [m. 47]. The cello probably takes the tune in the A minor stretch [m. 61-63].

listening_points.headline: A long stay in G major
listening_points.text: The music settles in G major at [m. 64], and stays there for a long stretch. Violin 1 mostly leads. Violin 2 probably leads at [m. 88-89]. Loud passages [m. 68-70] and [m. 82-89] alternate with soft ones. A crescendo is marked at [m. 73], leading to a loud moment at [m. 74].

listening_points.headline: Calm down, cello leads, then a new key
listening_points.text: The music turns soft at [m. 91]. The parts weave independent lines [m. 95-98]. The cello probably leads from [m. 99-102], with a crescendo marked at [m. 100]. The Allegro ends in F major [m. 105-106].

listening_points.headline: Part 3 begins, wandering through keys
listening_points.text: Part 3 starts softly in F major [m. 107]. It moves through A minor [m. 110] and back to F major [m. 114]. A crescendo at [m. 114-115] leads to a loud moment at [m. 116]. The first violin probably leads. This part is marked to be repeated.

listening_points.headline: Brighter keys: E major, A major, D major
listening_points.text: The cello probably takes the tune in E major, softly at first [m. 121-124], then loudly at [m. 125]. The key then brightens through A major [m. 129] and D major [m. 131]. Loud and soft alternate.

listening_points.headline: A dark C minor stretch, then G major
listening_points.text: The mood darkens in C minor [m. 137-146]. It starts soft, then turns loud at [m. 143]. The cello probably leads in G major at [m. 147-152].

listening_points.headline: C major returns, with sudden loud bursts
listening_points.text: C major returns at [m. 154], with Violin 1 leading softly. The volume jumps suddenly to loud at [m. 163], with independent lines in the loud stretch. The key moves to G major at [m. 172]. A computer estimate marks [m. 178] as the loudest and busiest point.

listening_points.headline: Settling into C major, cello leads before the end
listening_points.text: After brief D minor and A minor [m. 180-187], the music is back in C major [m. 188-221]. Violin 1 leads most of the time, with loud and soft contrasts. The cello probably leads at [m. 219-222] while a crescendo is marked. The key then turns to F major [m. 222].

listening_points.headline: Closing part: a quiet ending in C major
listening_points.text: The final part stays in C major [m. 227-246]. A crescendo at [m. 230] builds to loud at [m. 232]. The loud passage runs to [m. 240]. It then drops suddenly to soft at [m. 241]. The movement ends very softly at [m. 245-246], with all parts moving together.

glossary.explanation: A gradual rise in loudness. In the score it is marked cresc.
A sudden, sharp accent on a note.
The home note and scale that the music feels built around. Major keys usually sound brighter. Minor keys usually sound darker.
Each instrument plays its own line. No single tune stands out.
All the parts move together, with the same rhythm, like a hymn.
